title: AI Lead Generation Systems That Book Sales Calls

blocks.heading: Define a lead gen system
paragraphs: A system is trigger → enrichment → personalized outreach → booking → nurture → measurement. Random cold blasts are not systems; they burn domains and reputation. AI assists research, copy, and scoring—not bypassing consent laws. Goal is qualified calls on calendar, not vanity reply rates.
B2B service businesses and high-ticket coaches fit best. Productize for one ICP before expanding. Track cost per booked call and close rate. Ultimate tier includes system diagram worksheet.

blocks.heading: ICP and offer-market fit
paragraphs: Document firmographics, triggers, pain, budget, and decision maker. Offer must solve expensive problem: revenue, cost, risk, time. If close rate under fifteen percent, fix offer or ICP before more volume. Interview five recent buyers to extract language.
Claude synthesizes call notes into messaging doc. Avoid targeting 'everyone with a website'. Vertical focus improves reply quality. Tight ICP beats huge lists.

blocks.heading: Data sources and enrichment
paragraphs: Use Apollo, Clay, LinkedIn Sales Nav, or niche directories ethically. Enrich with tech stack, hiring signals, funding, content topics. Verify emails; bounce rates kill deliverability. Do not scrape against platform ToS.
Build lists in tiers: dream, fit, experiment. Refresh data quarterly; people change jobs. Ultimate includes enrichment prompt templates. Garbage in, garbage out.

blocks.heading: Scoring leads with AI
paragraphs: Score on fit, intent, and reachability. Claude reads company site and recent news for one-line relevance. Auto-skip industries you cannot serve. Human reviews top tier before send.
Scoring reduces wasted sends. Log why leads qualified or disqualified. Improve model rules weekly. Quality lists shrink but convert.

blocks.heading: Outbound channels that still work
paragraphs: Email primary for scale; LinkedIn for high-touch; calls for hot inbound. Multi-touch sequences over fourteen days. Each touch adds value: insight, audit, case snippet—not 'just checking in'. Warm calls booked via clear CTA link.
One channel mastered before adding others. Domain warmup for new email infrastructure. LinkedIn manual sends only—no banned automation. Compliance first.

blocks.heading: Copy that earns replies
paragraphs: Subject: specific to them, under seven words when possible. Opening: observation about their business. Body: problem hypothesis, micro proof, low-friction CTA. Ask one question or offer one useful asset.
Claude drafts variants; you personalize first line manually. Never fake mutual connections or meetings. A/B test subjects on small batches. Reply handling SOP within two hours.

blocks.heading: Booking infrastructure
paragraphs: Calendly or Cal.com with qualifying questions. Round-robin for teams. SMS reminder reduces no-shows. CRM stage updates on book.
Hide calendar link until reply interest. Two time options in email sometimes beat link. Track show rate, not just books. No-show follow-up sequence.

blocks.heading: Inbound magnets and AI-assisted content
paragraphs: Audit, calculator, or checklist lead magnets aligned to ICP. Landing page plus thank-you book CTA. Claude helps draft magnet and follow-up emails. Retarget site visitors with ethical pixels.
Magnets feed outbound retargeting. Quality magnet beats generic ebook. Promote in niche communities without spam. Measure magnet-to-call conversion.

blocks.heading: Nurture for not-yet-ready leads
paragraphs: Monthly value email for non-responders who opted in. Case studies and teardown content. Stop after sunset period. Re-engage campaigns quarterly.
Nurture protects long sales cycles. Segment by objection from replies. Claude drafts newsletter; you add original insight. Do not nurture people who unsubscribed.

blocks.heading: Handoff to sales
paragraphs: SDR qualifies on book; AE takes qualified. Brief card: company, pain, assets viewed, personalization notes. Recording optional with consent. SLA: contact within five minutes for inbound hot leads.
Bad handoff wastes gen spend. Feedback loop from sales to gen weekly. Disqualify criteria documented. RevOps mindset for small teams.

blocks.heading: Metrics dashboard
paragraphs: Emails sent, deliverability, reply rate, positive reply rate, meetings booked, show rate, pipeline, closed won. Cost per meeting and CAC payback. Channel comparison monthly. Kill sequences that underperform median.
Claude narrates weekly report. Share wins with team. Avoid optimizing reply rate alone—optimize revenue. Data beats gut.

blocks.heading: Compliance and reputation
paragraphs: CAN-SPAM, GDPR, CASL compliance. One-click unsubscribe. Honor do-not-contact immediately. Rotate domains responsibly; never spoof.
Ultimate includes compliance checklist. Legal for regulated industries. Reputation takes years to rebuild. Ethical gen compounds.

blocks.heading: Tool stack
paragraphs: CRM: HubSpot or Pipedrive. Sequencing: Instantly, Smartlead, or Apollo sequences. Enrichment: Clay workflows. Claude for research and copy drafting.
Keep stack under few tools. Integrate before adding new shiny app. Document API keys securely. Automate reporting last.

blocks.heading: Building productized lead gen for clients
paragraphs: Sell packaged '500 touches/month plus booking infra setup'. Charge setup plus monthly management. Report meetings booked transparently. Do not guarantee closed deals.
White-label for agencies with your SOP. Case studies require client permission. Raise prices when show rates prove out. Client success is your retention.

blocks.heading: 90-day implementation plan
paragraphs: Month 1: ICP, list build, sequence v1, booking flow. Month 2: send, measure, iterate copy and scoring. Month 3: add inbound magnet, nurture, hire VA for research. Targets vary—focus on learning speed.
Ultimate worksheets break weekly tasks. One vertical, one offer, one sequence first. Scale volume only after positive reply rate healthy. Systems beat heroics.
